chunks: And in the narration of Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you enter the Sacred Mosque, walk until you approach the Black Stone, then face it
and say: 'All praise is due to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us.'
Glory is to Allah, and praise is to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greater than His creation, and Allah is Greater than what I fear and dread.

'There is no god but Allah' alone, 'No partner for Him', 'To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise', 'He gives life and causes death', and He is Ever-Living who does not die, and He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good.
"And He is Able to do all things."
And send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and send peace upon the Messengers, as you did when you entered the Mosque.
Then say: 'O Allah, I believe in Your promise and I fulfill Your covenant.'
Then he mentioned as Muawiyyah mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and remembrances to recite when entering the Kaaba in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from Abu Basir, this hadith prescribes a specific ritual of dhikr upon entering Masjid al-Haram, linking the physical act of facing the Black Stone with spiritual acknowledgment of divine guidance. It emphasizes the transition from human limitation to divine grace, culminating in a reaffirmation of the covenant (*ahd*) with God, a theme deeply resonant in Shia devotional practice during Hajj and Umrah.
